He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State Nittany Lions]]. ==High school career== Stevens attended [[The Haverford School]] in [[Haverford Township, Pennsylvania]] for his sophomore and junior years. At Haverford, he was named to All-State and All-District teams both years, as well as leading Haverford to two straight state championship runs. During his senior season he attended [[Roman Catholic High School]] in [[Philadelphia]] where he played alongside future Penn State teammates, [[Tony Carr (basketball)|Tony Carr]] and Nazeer Bostick. During his senior year, Stevens was once again named to All-State and All-District teams, as well as All-Philadelphia. Roman Catholic dominated all season, ranking Number 1 in Pennsylvania and top 15 nationally, according to [[MaxPreps]]. Stevens scored 20 points on the way to winning the state championship game. ===Recruiting=== After the season, Stevens was ranked 100th on the [[ESPN]]'s Top 100 recruits of 2016 and third-ranked overall in Pennsylvania. {{College athlete recruit start|40=No|collapse=no|year=2016}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Lamar Stevens | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania|Philadelphia, PA]] | highschool = [[Roman Catholic High School|Roman Catholic]] (PA) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 215 | 40 = | commitdate = 09/18/15 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn grade = 80 | espn stars = 4 | grayshirt = }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = no | year = 2016 | rivals ref title = | scout ref title = | 247 ref title = | espn ref title = | rivals school = | scout s = | 247 school = | espn schoolid = | scout overall = | rivals overall = | 247 overall = | espn overall = | accessdate = | archivedate = | rivals archiveurl = | scout archiveurl = | 247 archiveurl = | espn archiveurl = | bball = yes }} ; Honors and Awards * ''3x [[Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association|PIAA]] AAAA All-State (2014, 2015, 2016)'' * ''2016 PIAA Class AAAA State Champions'' * ''2016 Philadelphia Player of the Year by the [[Philadelphia Daily News|Daily News]]'' * ''All-Philadelphia First Team (2016)'' * ''3x PIAA District 12 First Team (2014, 2015, 2016)'' ==College career== [[File:Lamar Stevens.jpg|thumb|right|175px|Stevens with [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] in 2017]] During Stevens' freshman season at Penn State, he started all 33 games for the Nittany Lions and was named Freshman of the Week multiple times with teammate [[Tony Carr (basketball)|Tony Carr]]. He was named as a First Team All-Freshman by the [[Big Ten]] and averaged over 12 points per game his first season. {{Cite news|url=http://www.pennlive.com/sports/index.ssf/2017/03/live_updates_from_penn_state_v_2.html|title=Penn State beats Nebraska, 76–67, in the Big Ten tournament: recap, final stats, photos|work=PennLive.com|access-date=July 28, 2017}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2017/03/michigan_state_thrashes_penn_s.html|title=Michigan State thrashes Penn State to open Big Ten Tournament|work=MLive.com|access-date=July 28, 2017|language=en-US}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2017/03/09/michigan-state-basketball/98972072/|title='Grown up' Michigan State destroys Penn State in Big Ten tournament|work=Detroit Free Press|access-date=July 28, 2017}} Stevens scored a season-high 30 points on January 5, 2018, against [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]].{{cite news |last1=Gery |first1=Ryne |title=Penn State's Lamar Stevens makes statement as one of Big Ten's best hybrid forwards |url=https://www.centredaily.com/sports/college/penn-state-university/psu-basketball/article193329049.html |access-date=December 11, 2019 |work=[[Centre Daily Times]] |date=January 6, 2018}} As a sophomore, Stevens averaged 15.5 points and 5.9 rebounds per game. He helped the Nittany Lions post a 26–13 record and win the NIT. Stevens was named Most Outstanding Player of the NIT.{{cite news |last1=Hunt |first1=Donald |title=Lamar Stevens named to Julius Erving Small Forward of the Year Award |url=https://www.phillytrib.com/sports/lamar-stevens-named-to-julius-erving-small-forward-of-the/article_4e93f286-2d93-5414-8687-e4741fb323b2.html |access-date=December 11, 2019 |work=[[The Philadelphia Tribune]] |date=October 19, 2018}} As a junior, Stevens averaged 19.9 points and 7.7 rebounds per game. He was named to the [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten Conference ]]first team by the media and earned second-team honors from the league's coaches. Stevens was an All-District VII second-team selection by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]].{{cite web |title=Men's basketball's Lamar Stevens named to 2019-20 preseason All-Big Ten (2020–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Stevens was signed by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] to a [[two-way contract]] on November 28, 2020.{{cite web|author=clemgold|title=Cavaliers Sign Lamar Stevens to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/lamar-stevens-signing-201128|website=NBA.com|date=November 28, 2020|access-date=November 19, 2020}} He made his NBA debut on December 28, 2020, in a 118–94 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He scored two points and collected two rebounds in five minutes of action.{{cite web|first=Tyler|last=Donohue|title=Former Penn State star Lamar Stevens scores in NBA debut|url=https://247sports.com/college/penn-state/Article/NBA-News-Cleveland-Cavaliers-rookie-Lamar-Stevens-scores-points-debut-157946480/|website=247sports.com|date=December 28, 2020|access-date=January 25, 2021}} On February 23, 2021, he scored eight points, including a game-winner, in a 112–111 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]]{{cite web|author=clejsykes|title=Cavaliers Sign Lamar Stevens to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/stevens-contract-210414|website=NBA.com|date=April 14, 2021|access-date=April 14, 2021}} and on April 14, he signed a multi-year contract with the Cavaliers. On January 12, 2022, Stevens scored a career and game high of 23 points in a 111–91 win over the Utah Jazz.{{cite news |title=Cavaliers 111-91 Jazz (Jan 12, 2022) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401360443/cavaliers-jazz |work=ESPN |language=en}} On July 6, 2023, Stevens was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] as part of a three-team trade with the [[Miami Heat]] and [[Cleveland Cavaliers]],{{cite web|author=sasmpolk|title=SAN ANTONIO COMPLETES THREE-TEAM TRADE WITH CLEVELAND AND
